Create a clean, production-ready character reference sheet based on the person in the reference image.

Use a wide horizontal canvas with a plain white or light neutral background and soft, even studio lighting.

On the left side, place one large, highly detailed bust portrait occupying about 40% of the canvas. The character must face directly toward the camera, with the head upright, eyes looking straight into the camera, mouth closed, and a calm neutral expression. Even if the reference image shows a different facial angle, pose, expression, or lighting, standardize this main portrait into a clear front-facing neutral identity view.

On the right side, place exactly three smaller full-body turnaround views of the same character, evenly spaced:
1. a strict front-facing full-body view,
2. a strict left-side full-body profile,
3. a strict back-facing full-body view.

All three full-body views must use a neutral standing pose only. The character must stand upright in a relaxed standard turnaround posture, with the arms resting naturally at the sides and the body clearly visible from head to toe. Do not use any action pose, dramatic pose, walking pose, twisting pose, contrapposto, hand-on-hip pose, raised-arm pose, leaning pose, or expressive body language. Do not let the character hold, swing, or present any prop in a way that changes the neutral standing posture.

Preserve the character’s exact facial identity and distinctive features, including face shape, forehead, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose bridge and tip, lips, jawline, chin, cheekbones, ears, skin tone, skin details, age, hairstyle, hairline, hair accessories, and overall appearance.

Preserve the same hairstyle, hair length, body proportions, costume design, fabric colors, clothing layers, sleeves, collar, waist details, accessories, footwear, and silhouette across all views. The front, side, and back designs must be logically consistent with one another.

Use realistic photographic detail, consistent scale, consistent anatomy, and consistent lighting across every view. Make it look like a practical character turnaround sheet for downstream character creation, not a fashion poster, cinematic scene, mood board, or decorative collage.

Create a realistic cinematic three-quarter full-body photograph of the character from the reference sheet standing in a lively outdoor night market.

Show one character only. The character should stand naturally with the body turned slightly away from the camera and the face turned approximately 45 degrees back toward the camera in a three-quarter view. Keep the head upright, the eyes looking toward the camera, the mouth closed, and the facial expression calm and neutral. The pose must remain simple and natural, with both arms resting naturally at the sides.

Preserve the character’s exact facial identity and distinctive facial structure, including the face shape, forehead, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose bridge and tip, lips, jawline, chin, cheekbones, ears, skin tone, skin details, age, hairstyle, hairline, hair accessories, and overall appearance.

Preserve the same body proportions, hairstyle, costume design, fabric colors, clothing layers, sleeves, waist details, accessories, footwear, and silhouette shown in the reference sheet.

Place the character in a bustling evening night market with warm lantern light, food stalls, hanging signs, soft ambient crowd lighting, and a lively market atmosphere in the background. Relight the character naturally to match the night market environment, using realistic warm highlights, soft shadows, natural contact shadows, atmospheric depth, and coherent environmental lighting. Show the entire body clearly from head to feet.

Create a realistic full-body photograph of the character from image 2 placed naturally into the scene in image 1.

Show one character only. Place the character standing beside the motorcycle in image 1, positioned naturally next to it, with one hand resting lightly on the handlebar. Keep the body upright in a calm neutral standing pose. The face should be turned slightly toward the camera with a calm neutral expression.

Preserve the character’s exact facial identity and distinctive features, including face shape, forehead, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose bridge and tip, lips, jawline, chin, cheekbones, ears, skin appearance, hairstyle, hairline, hair accessories, age, and overall appearance.

Preserve the same body proportions, hairstyle, costume design, fabric colors, clothing layers, sleeves, waist details, footwear, and silhouette shown in image 2.

Preserve the original composition, camera perspective, and environment of image 1. Match the character naturally to the motorcycle scene, with correct scale, correct foot placement on the ground, realistic contact with the handlebar, natural contact shadows, coherent perspective, and lighting consistent with the outdoor scene.

Create a realistic full-body photograph of the character from image 2 placed naturally into the scene in image 1.

Show one character only. Place the character standing beside the round café table in image 1, positioned naturally next to the table. Keep the body upright in a calm neutral standing pose, with both arms resting naturally at the sides or with one hand resting lightly near the edge of the table in a subtle natural way. The face should be turned slightly toward the camera with a calm neutral expression.

Preserve the character’s exact facial identity and distinctive features, including face shape, forehead, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose bridge and tip, lips, jawline, chin, cheekbones, ears, skin appearance, hairstyle, hairline, hair accessories, age, and overall appearance.

Preserve the original composition, camera perspective, furniture layout, and environment of image 1. Match the character naturally to the café interior, with correct scale, correct foot placement on the floor, realistic spatial relation to the table and chairs, natural contact shadows, coherent perspective, and lighting consistent with the afternoon indoor scene.

Change only the character’s tops.

Replace only the current top with a fitted white long-sleeve shirt.

Change only the color of the character’s tops.

Change the tops to pale beige.
Dress the person in image 1 with the outfit shown in image 2.

Replace the person’s current outfit with the clothing from image 2. Transfer the full outfit design as closely as possible

Preserve the person’s facial identity, hairstyle, expression, pose, body proportions, lighting, camera angle, and background from image 1.

Make the outfit fit naturally on the body, with realistic fabric folds, correct proportions, proper layering, and lighting consistent with the original image. Keep the clothing style, silhouette, colors, and accessories consistent with image 2.

Remove only the outer tops from the person in image 1.

Remove the outer jacket / blazer / coat while preserving a fully clothed appearance. Reveal and preserve the inner top underneath. Keep the lower garment, legwear, footwear, facial identity, hairstyle, expression, pose, body proportions, lighting, and background unchanged.

Reconstruct the newly revealed areas naturally, with realistic fabric continuation, correct body fit, and coherent lighting. Preserve the person’s modest, fully dressed appearance.

Replace the person in image 1 with the character from image 2.

Preserve the original pose, body position, head angle, gaze direction, facial expression, camera angle, framing, composition, environment, furniture, objects, perspective, and lighting of image 1.

Transfer the exact identity and character design from image 2, including the facial identity, face shape, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose structure, lips, jawline, hairstyle, hair accessories, age, body proportions, costume design, fabric colors, clothing layers, footwear, and overall appearance.

The character from image 2 should naturally inherit the pose and position of the original person in image 1. Match the character to the scene with realistic scale, anatomy, contact shadows, environmental lighting, and color temperature.
Replace only the facial identity of the person in image 1 with the facial identity of the character from image 2.

Transfer the character’s distinctive facial identity from image 2, including the face shape, forehead, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose bridge and tip, lips, jawline, chin, cheekbones, skin tone, skin texture, age, and recognizable facial features.

Preserve the original facial expression, gaze direction, eyelid position, mouth position, head angle, head pose, camera perspective, and lighting from image 1.

Preserve the original hairstyle, hairline placement, ears, headwear, neck, body, body proportions, clothing, accessories, pose, hands, background, composition, objects, depth of field, and overall color grading of image 1.

Blend the new facial identity naturally into the original head. Match the skin tone, facial shadows, highlights, sharpness, image grain, and environmental lighting of image 1. Keep the face anatomically realistic and correctly aligned with the original head angle.

Remove the original facial identity completely, but do not replace the entire head or person. Do not change the hairstyle, clothing, body, pose, expression, scene, or camera framing.

Dress the person in image 1 with the outfit shown in image 2.

Replace the person’s current outfit with the clothing from image 2. Transfer the full outfit design as closely as possible

Preserve the person’s facial identity, hairstyle, expression, pose, body proportions, lighting, camera angle, and background from image 1.

Make the outfit fit naturally on the body, with realistic fabric folds, correct proportions, proper layering, and lighting consistent with the original image. Keep the clothing style, silhouette, colors, and accessories consistent with image 2.
